amendments.because: Listing every test in the new fix's Done-when duplicates next's lines and grows without limit; the fix names the failed run instead
amendments.done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

done_when: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge fix start command for that failed run (or the started fix's next step)

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. A pytest failure such as `FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_mode[basic - legacy] - AssertionError` is reported as `tests/test_a.py::test_mode[basic`, so `forge next` does not name that failing test. The ` - ` delimiter in this regex also occurs inside valid parameter IDs. This is a distinct case from the settled space-ID finding: the proof covers `[previous release]`, which has no spaced hyphen. [Pytest documents that parameter IDs identify failing cases](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/example/parametrize.html).
findings.title: Not done: parameter IDs containing spaced hyphens are truncated

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 3, Harm 2
The parser accepts only pytest-style `FAILED` or `ERROR` lines containing `::`. A scheduled Vitest or Go job can fail with named tests in its log while `forge next` lists only the job. The named proof supplies pytest output only. The shipped guidance supports these runners; this additional language case remains open.
findings.title: Follow-up: name JavaScript and Go test failures in scheduled runs

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
The query reads only the newest 100 scheduled runs across all workflows. A workflow scheduled every five minutes can fill that page in about eight hours, hiding a failed daily workflow whose latest run is older. The coordinator explicitly narrowed this case to a follow-up; the proof uses only three runs.
findings.title: Follow-up: retain failed daily workflows beyond the recent-run page

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): back to one GitHub request — recent scheduled runs (per page 100), newest per workflow id — so next stays fast with many workflows; alerts key by workflow id. A very frequent schedule crowding out a daily run is a follow-up.

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
